To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) explanations of machine learning models are related with selecting feature value pairs that are sufficient for the predictions, (2) explanations of machine models are related with the explanations of the predictions of the models.
the explanations of machine learning models are not only important, but also can be generated efficiently and accurately.

(a) the explanations generated using the proposed approach were found to be useful in the task of identifying the most relevant features, and (b) the explanations generated by the proposed approach were more accurate than the explanations generated by other state-of-the-art methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why and when explanations of machine learning models should be used in practice.
the question of whether the explanations of machine learning (ML) models are useful for the end-user.
the problem of generating explanations for the predictions of a machine learning (ML) model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the “why not?” explanation is more useful in terms of the user’s understanding of the ML model, while the “why” explanation has the advantage of being able to be used in the context of other tasks.
the use of the Why-why-not approach to explain machine learning models is a promising and effective method, but it is not a panacea and it has its limitations and challenges.
the “why not?” question is not a good way of explaining the results of a machine learning model. It can only be used in very limited cases and even then it can lead to misleading results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “why not” explanation is more informative than the “why” explanation.
it provides a new framework for explaining ML models, and it can be used to explain models that are not explainable by existing methods.

we are able to explain a model's prediction for a given instance by finding a minimal set of rules that is sufficient for the prediction, while also providing a human interpretable explanation of the model's prediction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the explanations generated by the Why-Not? model are more useful to the end user.
we can use explanations to understand the behavior of a model.
the explanations for why the model made its prediction are not necessarily the same as the explanations for why it didn’t make the same prediction on another instance.
